headline: Spirex: Open-source, self-hostable Jira alternative for agile engineering teams
summary: Spirex offers sprint boards, backlog, epics, and custom workflows without per-feature upsells. It's free, AGPL-3.0 licensed, and includes a 5-minute Jira import.
details: Spirex is a new free, open-source, self-hostable alternative to Jira, designed for agile engineering teams. It provides essential features like sprint boards, backlog management, epics, and custom columns.
The tool aims to offer the full workflow engineering teams need without the common per-feature upsells found in other solutions. It also includes robust reporting capabilities.
A key feature is its 5-minute Jira importer, which can bring over existing projects and comments seamlessly. Spirex is still in its early stages and welcomes community feedback.
Licensed under AGPL-3.0, Spirex supports self-hosting via Docker and Kubernetes, ensuring no vendor lock-in. A live demo is available for testing without signup.
caption:
Tired of Jira's feature lock-ins and per-feature upsells? A new free, open-source, self-hostable alternative, Spirex, is here for agile teams.

Spirex is a new free, open-source, self-hostable alternative to Jira, designed for agile engineering teams. It provides essential features like sprint boards, backlog management, epics, and custom columns.

The tool aims to offer the full workflow engineering teams need without the common per-feature upsells found in other solutions. It also includes robust reporting capabilities.

A key feature is its 5-minute Jira importer, which can bring over existing projects and comments seamlessly. Spirex is still in its early stages and welcomes community feedback.

Licensed under AGPL-3.0, Spirex supports self-hosting via Docker and Kubernetes, ensuring no vendor lock-in. A live demo is available for testing without signup.

headline: Build a Python tool to scan and revoke risky ERC-20 token allowances
summary: Accumulated ERC-20 token allowances create a silent attack surface, allowing compromised contracts to drain your wallet. This Python scanner helps detect and revoke risky approvals before an incident occurs.
details: Every time you interact with DeFi protocols, you grant ERC-20 token allowances, giving smart contracts permission to spend your tokens. Most users accumulate dozens of these approvals, often with unlimited amounts, creating a significant security risk.

A compromised contract with an active allowance can drain your crypto wallet without needing your private key. This automated Python scanner audits every approval across your address, identifies risky ones, and generates revocation transactions.

The tool queries the Etherscan API for Approval events across all ERC-20 tokens, decoding spender, amount, and token contract data. It then classifies these allowances to pinpoint potential vulnerabilities.

The average DeFi user has 15–30 active token approvals, many of which are unlimited. High-profile exploits, such as the Multichain hack and various phishing campaigns, have exploited this exact vulnerability vector.

This open-source tool provides crucial visibility and control over your digital assets, enabling you to proactively manage your security posture. The complete script is available on GitHub for immediate use.
